> So, first of all, I REALLY like the number 42, so its gonna be like everwhere! As for what the parent communicator 42 actually does though, it will let parents let their kids know that they need them. I have my room upstairs and am almost always in it, so when my parents need me to come down, they have to yell for me. This will allow them to click a button downstairs, a corresponding device in my room will start beeping a very obnoxious noise. This can help me when they need me to wake up(I am a very heavy sleeper and they need to wake me up... T-T) or just to call me down for a meal like dinner. Essentially, it will be a child summoner... The kid will be able to interact with their part of the design as well, turning on do not disturb and such. This can be bypassed through the parent module but I am hoping it gives a moment for the parent to consider if they actually want to call their child at that time. Both modules will have a battery and will charge with usbc. I am hoping I can use something like suction to stick them to a wall so it doesnt take up too much space. It might also be able to double as a PA system so the parents can communicate things other than just an alarm of sorts.

First, I started research on how I can make my 2 modules communicate. This is the most essential part as this is how the main goal will be reached.

currently, I have found ESP Now which seems promising. I was thinking about looking into ESP 32s anyway.

The next issue is: how will the circuits be wired? Let's lay out our basic circuit requirements for the PC42 (parent communicator 42) so that the P(parent) and C(child) modules line up(it's also really cool that the C module matches the overall name while meaning something else :D ).

# P Module

* must be able to send a signal to C module to turn on an alarm.
* PA system for more intricate messages.
* Case detection such as a DND bypass(might be more on code side, but we need a way say yes or no to bypassing that doesn't involve the alarm or PA button)
* Support for decent microphone for the PA system.
* battery life for at least 2 days without charge
* small form factor(thinking 6x6 inches max)
* button for child to turn off the alarm to verify they made it downstairs

Additional notes: I am writing all of this in real time to document my thinking, so I am thinking we can just have some LEDs to indicate when the DND is on and for other things we might need.

# C Module
* Support for snooze button that snoozes for 2-5 minutes at a time and will lock until the next day
* Good speaker for PA system
* small form factor(thinking 6x6 inches max)
* possible alarm clock for waking up before parents, same idea applies about going down to turn off

So, its currently 12 am, but i slept for like 6 hours after coming home from school :) so I wont go crazy this time. Im sorry for whoever had to deal with my mental breakdown yesterday but im good now. I can do this. This session, I want to finish the PCBs for the two modules so let's get started.

First, we need to figure out where all of the things will be connected.

# General Connections

We will start with the general connections for both modules

## Speaker system
Let's start with the speaker system because it is the heart of the project.

So the Speaker amp needs 5 inputs.
* Power - This will be 3v3
* Ground - ground :P
* DIN - We will use D0 to send data
* LRC - We will use D1 for the left-right clock
* BCLK - We will use D2 for the bit clock

The Xiao's pinout is so flexible :)

Then, the speaker will be connected to the screw terminal block on the breakout Amp.  I've had some weird experiences with screw terminals and the wires slip out a lot... I don't know if I didn't screw it in fully but i need to figure out a way to combat this.

for the schematic and footprint, I will use a 7x1 connector to represent the amp board.

# P Module
Now, for the P Module :)

## Mic

First, let's the mic. The mic has 6 pins.
* Power - 3v3
* ground - ground
* SD - the serial data will be on D3
* SCK - the serial clock will be D5
* WS - word select will be on D4
* LR - Left /Right will be connected to ground

I will use 2 1x3 connectors for the Mic.

The Microphone has been finished wiring :)

The wiring is so straight forward its so nice. Firmware might be hell idk...

## Buttons
Next, we can do the buttons.

The buttons are 4 pin, I will use a 4 pin symbol for them. For the 3d printed keycaps, I might use some glue to stick them on. There also might be some solution I can incorporate in the case such as how phone cases click the phone buttons while being physically connected to the case itself(unlike mechanical keyboard caps).

For the P module, we need
* Child off switch
* Alarm Button
* PA push-to-talk

### 2026-10-10 – HI! I'm back and I have less than 48 hours to do 8 hours of work. I'm hoping I can get 3-4 hours today and I can finish the last 4 hours tomorrow. So... First of all, I realized that we don't actually

**3.67h**

HI! I'm back and I have less than 48 hours to do 8 hours of work. I'm hoping I can get 3-4 hours today and I can finish the last 4 hours tomorrow. So... First of all, I realized that we don't actually need 2 speakers. We  need a microphone on the P module and a speaker on the C module. I also need 4 digit display for my alarm system, so we can substitute the speaker for that.

After looking for a bit, I couldn't find any 4 digit displays that were in budget, so I was thinking about scrapping the alarm system. We could probably find better buttons for the 5 buttons we need.

* PA button on P module - D6
* Alarm button on P module - D7
* Child turn off button on P module - D8
* Snooze button on C module -D9
* DND button on C module - D10

so... let's find some buttons!

On a side note, I was thinking we could cut costs on PCBs by making the thing modular. By having 1 firmware and all of the ports, we could just plug the buttons into the right place, and designate which one is which in the firmware! This way, all of the functions would work the same and we would get 5 PCBs from JLC and all of them would work!

The buttons I found were these:  https://www.adafruit.com/product/4431

The total is now $59 which means we might be able to cover PCB costs, or anything else that I have currently forgotten :)

I was looking at current requirements and the speaker amp needs a lot, so i will move it to 5v.
Everything else looks fine :)

We have 5 buttons left, and 5 input pins left as well! it is a perfect fit. I am kinda sad that I can't do the time based alarm but I think the overall goal was still achieved which is amazing.

The buttons have 3 wires:
* GND
* D - digital input
* POWER - 3v3

The symbols and footprint will be the generic 1x3 socket.

Now, for the extra costs :(

So first, we need connector sockets for the jumper wires. This is 5 1x3 sockets which is around $1.65.

My brother did the Stardance Hackpad mission and has left over LEDs so I can just add one in there for the DND indicator.

This is the 1x3 connectors: https://www.peconnectors.com/female-headers-pcb-1x-row-.100/hws8519/

Total is now $61.43 :)

Now, I was thinking. The buttons take up 5 digital slots, how will we add the LED? so after some research, I am going to put it in the same D pin as the DND button, but since they are on different modules, they will never be connected at the same time. This is kinda risky, but I don't want to cut the DND feature.

I finished the schematic :)

While making the pcb, I realized the routing was weird. Luckily I figured out my schematic was a little messed up because of the symbol switches i did for the mic. That couldve been bad :)

OK SO I FINISHED MY PCB :)

Features:

* Fully modular
    * Button placement is optional
    * Mic placement is optional
    * Speaker placement is optional
    * LED placement is optional
* PA System with microphone and speakers
* Alarm System with snooze, on, and off buttons

BOM has been minimized and all components have been accounted for I think.
